# pai code

Map a repository: symbols, callers and blast radius

```
pai code <command>
```

The code graph indexes a repository's definitions and references into PAI's own database (Postgres, or SQLite as fallback). It reads TypeScript/TSX, JavaScript, Swift and Python; other files get a file row only. The index is reconciled with the repo whenever you query it; a first index of an unindexed repo is started in the background (one at a time) when a session opens there, and after each worker merge. Edits are only marked; the next query re-reads them.

```sh
pai code index
pai code explore how does the router pick a provider
pai code callers resolveRoot
```

See also: `pai memory search`, `pai kg`

### pai code index

Index a repository

```
pai code index [ROOT] [options]
```

Scans the files git tracks (up to 1 MB each, skipping node_modules, dist, build and vendor) and stores their symbols and references. Only changed files are re-read unless you pass --force.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ROOT` | no | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--force` | flag | — | Re-read every file |
| `--root DIR` | string | — | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |
| `--json` | flag | — | Output raw JSON |

```sh
pai code index
pai code index ~/dev/my-repo --force
```

See also: `pai code status`

### pai code explore

Answer a question about the code in one call

```
pai code explore QUERY... [options]
```

Finds the definitions that match your question or symbol names and prints their source, callers and blast radius within a token budget. Indexes the repo first if needed.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `QUERY...` | yes | A question or symbol names |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root DIR` | string | — | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |
| `--budget TOKENS` | number | 4000 | Output budget in tokens |
| `--depth N` | number | — | How far to follow calls |
| `--json` | flag | — | Output raw JSON |

```sh
pai code explore ensureFresh
pai code explore where are sessions routed --budget 8000
```

See also: `pai code search`, `pai code impact`

### pai code search

Find symbols by name

```
pai code search QUERY... [options]
```

Lists definitions whose name matches the query.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `QUERY...` | yes | Part of a symbol name |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root DIR` | string | — | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |
| `--limit N` | number | 20 | Maximum results |
| `--json` | flag | — | Output raw JSON |

```sh
pai code search tunnel
pai code search Storage --limit 5 --json
```

See also: `pai code explore`

### pai code impact

What a change to a symbol could break

```
pai code impact NAME [options]
```

Follows callers outward to the given depth and lists the affected files and symbols.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | Symbol name |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root DIR` | string | — | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |
| `--depth N` | number | 2 | How many caller levels to follow |
| `--json` | flag | — | Output raw JSON |

```sh
pai code impact resolveRoot
pai code impact resolveRoot --depth 3
```

See also: `pai code callers`

### pai code summarize

Write module and repo summaries with the local model

```
pai code summarize [options]
```

For every module (a directory with source files) and the repo, stores a short summary: purpose (written by the local model from signatures, doc comments and top references), entry points, what it depends on and what depends on it. Runs at background priority, one module at a time, and never uses a cloud model; it stops with an error when no local model is running. A module is regenerated only when its source changed (--force redoes all). Summaries are also stored as memory chunks, so the next embed pass makes them searchable with memory search.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root DIR` | string | — | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |
| `--project SLUG` | string | — | A registered project instead of the current repo |
| `--all` | flag | — | Every registered project whose code graph is already indexed |
| `--changed` | flag | true | Only modules whose source changed since their summary (default) |
| `--force` | flag | — | Regenerate every summary |
| `--max-minutes N` | number | — | Start no new module after N minutes |
| `--json` | flag | — | Output raw JSON |

```sh
pai code summarize
pai code summarize --project pai --changed
pai code summarize --all --max-minutes 90
```

See also: `pai code summary`, `pai code explore`

### pai code summary

Show the stored summary of a module or repo

```
pai code summary TARGET [options]
```

Prints the summary for a key (code:<slug>:<path>), a directory or a file path; a path without its own summary falls back to the enclosing module, then the repo. Use . for the repo.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TARGET` | yes | Key, directory or file path |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root DIR` | string | — | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |
| `--json` | flag | — | Output raw JSON |

```sh
pai code summary src/codegraph
pai code summary code:pai:src/router
pai code summary .
```

See also: `pai code summarize`, `pai code explore`

### pai code relate

Derive relations between projects and notes

```
pai code relate [options]
```

Reads the code graphs of the indexed registered projects and writes relations to the knowledge graph (kg_triples): depends-on (manifests), calls-api (routes and MCP tools another project registers), calls-cli (`pai <verb>` / `aibroker <verb>` invocations), shares-protocol (same message types), duplicates (near-identical functions) and, from the vault notes, mentions and cites. A relation that disappears gets an end date, never deleted. Index the projects first (pai code index).

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--project SLUG` | string | — | Write only this project's relations (all projects are still read) |
| `--all` | flag | — | All registered projects and the notes (the default) |
| `--json` | flag | — | Output raw JSON |

```sh
pai code relate
pai code relate --project my-app
```

See also: `pai graph related`, `pai code index`

### pai code status

Show what is indexed for a repository

```
pai code status [ROOT] [options]
```

Prints whether the repo is indexed, the counts, languages, last full index, files marked dirty by edits, and an index running now. Does not index anything.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ROOT` | no | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--root DIR` | string | — | Repository root (default: the repo around the current directory) |
| `--json` | flag | — | Output raw JSON |

```sh
pai code status
pai code status ~/dev/my-repo --json
```

See also: `pai code index`
